why: The independent whole for DESIGN.md §10 criterion 12. Every instrumented surface the EP exposes in production Rust, and what the wiring census does about it. Read ci/check_census_completeness.py first: this file is the map, not the screen. An entry here is a claim by a named owner, and a surface with no entry fails the screen — which is the only reason the count can ever be wrong.
not_a_closure: A PASS from the screen means every surface is accounted for, NOT that the census covers them. The 'uncensused' entries below are the standing gaps and they are the evidence that criterion 12 is not met. Trinity owns row 12's tally.

Selects the packed GEMV path. Investigated 2026-08-02: the switch is resolved in rust/src/ops/quant.rs:345 and enters the program as SPECIALIZATION CONSTANT index 5 of q_gemv.comp, and rust/src/vk/pipeline.rs keys the pipeline cache on (shader_stem, spec_constants) — so the two settings really are two different pipelines. But NO artifact this project produces records a pipeline key or a spec constant: trace.rs's Phase set has PipelineLookup and no payload, and no counter names the variant. So a host-side record of the env var would not close this: R10 asks for an artifact the mechanism PRODUCED whose content varies with its input, and reading env::var from a harness proves nothing about what the EP did with it. UNTIL an EP-side change records the resolved value (or the pipeline key) in an artifact, every kernel observation we hold is silent about which kernel it observed. Owed by Mouse (ops/) with Switch (vk/pipeline.rs): emit the spec-constant vector, or the resolved gemv_packed bool, into the trace or the counters.

Kill switch for the DESIGN.md §8.11 graph-level rank inference pass; set to 0 and every claim predicate sees exactly the ranks ORT reported, unset and the conservative Shape/Cast/Concat overlay runs first. Sole reader is rank_inference_enabled() at rust/src/logging.rs:432, consumed once per GetCapability by infer_graph_shapes() in rust/src/ep.rs. It landed UNMAPPED in PR #46 (issue #8) and this entry is the correction, not a coverage claim: the screen was right, the switch was the thing that was wrong, and PR #46's CI never completed (GitHub Actions outage) so nothing caught it before merge. NOT censused, and deliberately not recorded as such. The census graph is a six-node Add/Mul elementwise chain that the EP claims in full and whose every edge ORT already ranks, so the pass has nothing to prove in that frame; an armed/unarmed pair would read 'no difference', which is a 0 for an event that cannot occur (R12) and would read as evidence the switch is inert. That is the same reachability defect ONNXRUNTIME_EP_VULKAN_GEMV_PACKED and the CLAIM_DEBUG census segment already carry. The switch IS discriminated today, but by instruments outside this screen's frame that must not be laundered into it: tests/ops/test_rank_inference_chain.py pairs it 0/unset across ten graph-level cases (unknown rank, symbolic dims, non-integral Cast, incompatible ranks, out-of-range axis, mixed known/unknown lengths, Shape start/end, fanout, cycles), and rust/tools/probe_model_op_census.py A/Bs it on checksum-pinned bertsquad-12 where dispatches_executed moves 4 -> 367 and claimed nodes 481 -> 489 (bench/results/rank8/). Neither is one of test_wiring_census.py's mechanisms. Owed by Mouse, and only two things close it: (a) give the census lane one deliberately unranked chain -- Shape -> Cast(FLOAT) -> Slice -> Squeeze -> Cast(INT32) -> Unsqueeze -> Concat -> Cast(INT64) -> Reshape, the BERT shape, with a MatMul anchor so the net-benefit gate does not decline the island for unrelated reasons -- and read claimed_nodes or dispatches_executed across the pair; or (b) publish the pass's own arithmetic as a C ABI counter (ranks_proved / extents_proved exist in rust/src/shape_infer.rs Stats but reach only a log line, never an artifact), after which the pair becomes a two-arm discriminator like DEVICE_MEMORY's without touching the census graph at all.
Raises logging to Info. Unobserved by the census.

Sticky per-process VK_ERROR_DEVICE_LOST count, incremented at rust/src/vk/cmd.rs:333 on a fence wait. No wiring-census mechanism reads it, and none could without a change: the census's own graph is a six-node elementwise chain that never provokes a device loss, so a mechanism added today would read a permanent 0/0 in that frame — the same reachability defect ONNXRUNTIME_EP_VULKAN_GEMV_PACKED already carries. It is not unobserved everywhere: rust/tools/device_loss_gate.py reads device_losses off every repetition's own counters snapshot and records rec['lost'] across paired arms that provoke it on purpose (device-memory budget clamp, KV arena pin — bench/results/device_loss_gate_armB_budget.json, ci/device_loss_incident_records.json), and test_wiring_census.py::test_the_counters_mirror_matches_the_running_dll reads it to prove the ctypes ABI mirror has not drifted (the 2026-08-02 mid-struct insertion incident this field caused). Neither is the census: the gate is a standalone incident tool and the mirror test checks an offset, not a state. Closing this needs a census mechanism that provokes a device loss inside the census's own graph, or one that adopts device_loss_gate's evidence as its observation — owed by Switch.

Fused-node outputs ORT allocated in this EP's own device memory, incremented via record_output_residency() called from rust/src/vk/session.rs:2981. No wiring-census mechanism reports it, and the census's clean/inject/flags arms never arm ONNXRUNTIME_EP_VULKAN_DEVICE_MEMORY, so ORT never has a device allocator to hand this field a nonzero reading in that frame. A real capture exists outside the census: bench/results/probe_kv_device_residency.py and bench/results/probe_default_bind_outputs.py both read this field into their written artifacts (bench/results/kv_device_residency-*.json, default_bind_outputs-dev{0,1}.json) across multiple arms, but no test asserts on its value or on it varying — it is captured, not checked. Closing this needs either a census arm that arms the device allocator, or a test on the existing archival artifact that asserts the value moves with the arm — owed by Switch.

Fused-node outputs ORT allocated in host memory, incremented via record_output_residency() called from rust/src/vk/session.rs:2981 (see outputs_device_resident, its complement). No wiring-census mechanism reports it. bench/results/probe_kv_device_residency.py and bench/results/probe_default_bind_outputs.py capture it into their artifacts across arms, but neither that capture nor any test asserts on its value or on it varying with the arm — it is the one member of the outputs_device_resident/outputs_host_resident/outputs_device_bound triple with no assertion anywhere in the tree, only presence in archival JSON. Owed by Switch: either a census arm, or a test on the existing artifact.

Fused-node outputs bound directly to ORT's device buffer at Step 1c, incremented at rust/src/vk/session.rs:1805. This is the strongest-evidenced of the thirteen: tests/ops/test_kv_device_residency.py asserts counters['outputs_device_bound'] > 0 in the EP-bind lane, == 0 in the caller-bind lane, and that the two differ (lines 133, 155-157) — a genuine, non-vacuous, per-lane falsifier over committed artifacts (bench/results/kv_device_residency-{callerbind,epbind}.json). bench/results/probe_default_bind_outputs.py and bench/results/probe_kv_device_residency.py both also use it as a live route discriminator (the lane a run took is read off this field, never off ONNXRUNTIME_EP_VULKAN_BIND_OUTPUTS — rust/src/vk/session.rs:782 says so explicitly). None of this is the wiring census: test_kv_device_residency.py is a separate module, not one of test_wiring_census.py's fourteen mechanisms, and the census's own graph never arms the device allocator that makes this field nonzero. So it remains an uncensused surface from this screen's frame even though it is one of the best-tested counters in the repository outside that frame. Closing it inside the census needs a census arm that arms ONNXRUNTIME_EP_VULKAN_DEVICE_MEMORY and ONNXRUNTIME_EP_VULKAN_BIND_OUTPUTS together — owed by Switch.

Nodes claimed on a §8.9 ledger entry whose device cannot be compared to this run's hardware, incremented at rust/src/registry.rs:3827 (record_device_unattributed, called only on a hit, never on a miss). No wiring-census mechanism reports it; ledger_lookup (test_wiring_census.py lines ~1910-1957) is the mechanism that reads the neighbouring ledger fields (proven_key_lookups, ledger_hits, ledger_entries, unproven_declines, unproven_forms_claimed) but its observation string never mentions this field or its two siblings below, so adding a census arm that exercises the ledger does not by itself make this one censused. rust/src/disclosure.rs aggregates the per-session count into Disclosure::device_unattributed and discloses it per form at INFO (disclosure.rs:117, 213-215), and rust/tools/probe_session_disclosure.py captures the raw counter into bench/results/session-disclosure-*.json — but nothing asserts on it varying; it is disclosed to a log and archived, never checked. Owed by Mouse: extend ledger_lookup's observation to name this field (and the two below), or add a disclosure-side test asserting it moves with a planted unattributable-device entry.

Nodes claimed on a §8.9 ledger entry that is sound about this exact subject but was proven in a different frame (different device or shader compiler), incremented at rust/src/registry.rs:3834-3838 (record_proven_elsewhere_claim). Same gap as device_unattributed_claims and the same reason: ledger_lookup's observation string (test_wiring_census.py) does not name this field, rust/src/disclosure.rs discloses the aggregate per form at INFO (disclosure.rs:117, 600) and rust/tools/probe_session_disclosure.py archives the raw count, but no test in the tree asserts this counter is nonzero or moves with an arm. §8.9.19 part 1 turned this from a silent decline into a disclosed claim specifically so an operator could see it without reading a counters file; the census still cannot see it. Owed by Mouse: name it in ledger_lookup's observation, or add a disclosure test with a planted proven-elsewhere entry.

Nodes declined because the §8.9 ledger entry's subject moved (kernel replaced, or SPIR-V differs with no source_digest to attribute it), incremented at rust/src/registry.rs:3771 (record_subject_changed_decline). Not read by ledger_lookup's observation string, and not the same thing as rust/tools/probe_ledger_subject_check.py, which is a real and rigorous falsifier (7 arms, MEASURED incident 2026-08-03 where a GQA shader edit without a ledger regen declined all 32 GroupQueryAttention nodes and only this field saw it) — but that tool asserts on gen_proof_ledger.py --check's own text output (a build-time ledger validator), never on this runtime counter. rust/src/disclosure.rs's Disclosure::subject_changed aggregates the per-session count (disclosure.rs:230, 412) and warrants a WARN, and rust/tools/probe_session_disclosure.py archives the raw count, but nothing asserts on this exact counter moving. Owed by Mouse: name it in ledger_lookup's observation, or add a runtime-counter assertion alongside the existing --check text assertion in probe_ledger_subject_check.py.

Disables the Step 1c output-side device bind; read once at rust/src/vk/session.rs:768 (output_bind_requested), default ON since 2026-08-03. flag_frame (test_wiring_census.py) is the mechanism that discloses nine other switches and does not include this one. The switch's own doc comment (session.rs:782) is explicit that a census must read outputs_bind_attempted/outputs_device_bound off the run rather than read this variable, which is exactly what tests/ops/test_kv_device_residency.py does (asserting outputs_device_bound differs between the callerbind and epbind lanes) and what bench/results/probe_kv_device_residency.py and bench/results/probe_default_bind_outputs.py do as multi-arm falsifiers; bench/results/criterion10_route-dev{0,1}-*.json is the route-identity evidence (forced on, all 65 per-output residuals identical to the unbound route on both vendors — Round 35). None of that is the wiring census's own frame. Owed by Switch: extend flag_frame to name this switch, using outputs_device_bound as the discriminator rather than the env value itself, per the switch's own documented reading rule.

Named exactly once in the whole tree, inside a doc comment at rust/src/ep.rs:1631 (introduced by commit b602bbb as prose only, `git log -S` finds no other occurrence ever). No `std::env::var` call anywhere in rust/src reads this name; the extractor found it only because the name appears inside backticks in a comment describing a one-off manual measurement session. There is no switch here for a census to observe because there is nothing in the shipped binary that reads it — not a standing gap, a name with no implementation behind it.

The device-memory ceiling this process imposes on itself, in MB; read at rust/src/vk/host_device_memory.rs:100 (budget_bytes), a fault-injection instrument for the device-allocator degrade-to-host-staging path. Not one of flag_frame's nine switches. rust/tools/device_loss_gate.py arms it as one of two knobs (with ONNXRUNTIME_EP_VULKAN_KV_ARENA) that provoke device_losses on purpose (bench/results/device_loss_gate_armB_budget.json), and bench/results/probe_device_memory_hazards.py exercises it directly, but neither is the wiring census and the census's own clean/inject/flags arms never set it. Owed by Switch: a census arm pinning a small budget alongside a read of device_losses/alloc_failed_lookups.

A planted control (rust/src/logging.rs:63) that makes every stderr write from this process report failure without writing, so the §8.9.7 disclosure escalation path can be observed firing on a shipping binary without needing a host whose stderr is genuinely closed. Not one of flag_frame's nine switches. rust/tools/probe_disclosure_reachability.py is a real, rigorous falsifier for it ("ARM 3 — ESCALATION (PLANTED)": with ORT's default threshold refusing INFO and stderr refusing the bytes, the disclosure must arrive at WARNING on ORT's own sink, and every run under this variable is marked stderr_fault_injection=ACTIVE in its own artifact — bench/results/disclosure-reachability-dev{0,1}-escalation.json), but that probe is not the wiring census. Owed by Mouse (§8.9.7 claim-disclosure delivery, same domain as ONNXRUNTIME_EP_VULKAN_CLAIM_DEBUG above): extend flag_frame or add a tenth census segment that reads probe_disclosure_reachability's own arm structure.

Declares the caller-bound-arena KV convention (present IS past, true length carried by seqlens_k alone); the sole reader is kv_arena_enabled() at rust/src/factory.rs:517-527, ships OFF. Not one of flag_frame's nine switches, and the census's six-node elementwise graph carries no KV cache at all, so it is not reachable from that frame regardless — the same shape as ONNXRUNTIME_EP_VULKAN_GEMV_PACKED's unreachability. It is nonetheless one of the most heavily evidenced switches in the repository outside the census: bench/results/probe_kv_arena_phi35.py, probe_kv_chain_phi35.py, probe_kv_lever_ledger.py and rust/tools/device_loss_gate.py all arm it directly against real Phi-3.5 KV chains (bench/results/kv_arena_chain-*.json, kv_arena_budget.json). Owed by Mouse (KV-cache op contract) with Switch (the bind-time alias check): a census lane that includes a KV-cache-shaped subgraph, or a discrimination arm in the existing archival probes.

The growing-cache prefix alias (stage past into present's prefix, never allocate a separate past buffer); the sole reader is kv_prefix_alias_enabled() at rust/src/factory.rs:554-561, ships ON — polarity reversed from every other flag in the file because disabling it is the escape hatch. Not one of flag_frame's nine switches, and unreachable from the census's KV-free graph for the same reason ONNXRUNTIME_EP_VULKAN_KV_ARENA is. bench/results/probe_ctx4096_shipping_lane.py is a real falsifier across shipping/noalias arms and context lengths (MEASURED 2026-08-04: the default shipping lane executes 355 dispatches at past_len 2048 and zero at 3072 with the alias off — bench/results/ctx4096_BEFORE.json), but it is an archival probe, not the wiring census. Owed by Mouse (KV-cache op contract) with Switch (the staging copy): a KV-cache-shaped census lane, or a discrimination arm in the existing archival probe.

mechanism_names.name_asserts: that graph nodes were grouped into islands by a partitioning decision, not merely claimed one by one
mechanism_names.discriminator: an observation that differs between a run that merges and a run that does not — islands_offered strictly below claimed_nodes on a graph with more than one fusible node

mechanism_names.name_asserts: that the identity case (one island per node) is detected and is an explicit red state
mechanism_names.discriminator: a run in which claimed == islands with both > 1, showing RED rather than VACUOUS

mechanism_names.name_asserts: that a NET BENEFIT was computed and decided the retention, not that a counter incremented
mechanism_names.discriminator: two runs with different cost-model env inputs producing different retention decisions on the same graph

mechanism_names.name_asserts: that GPU work was traced — device-side spans, not host spans emitted around a submit
mechanism_names.discriminator: an observation naming the phases emitted, and differing with ONNXRUNTIME_EP_VULKAN_TRACE_GPU set versus unset

mechanism_names.name_asserts: that MODEL outputs were compared and found equivalent, with the frame that executed them named
mechanism_names.discriminator: a verdict carrying executed_by, differing between a run the EP executed and a run it declined

mechanism_names.name_asserts: that viable islands were RETAINED by a decision, distinct from no island being offered at all
mechanism_names.discriminator: a run where islands were offered and rejected, distinguishable from one where none was offered

mechanism_names.name_asserts: that a claim was checked against a ledger entry that exists independently of the claim table
mechanism_names.discriminator: a lookup that MISSES — ledger_hits strictly below proven_key_lookups on a key the ledger does not hold

mechanism_names.name_asserts: that a validation-layer message was CARRIED to the host, not that the layer was installed
mechanism_names.discriminator: the planted-violation arm reporting a different token from the clean arm

mechanism_names.name_asserts: that the layering rule was enforced over the whole crate
mechanism_names.discriminator: a planted layering violation outside src/ops/ turning the observation from PASS to a failure — on 2026-08-01 it did not

mechanism_names.name_asserts: that a broken commitment produced a WARNING on the channel a user would see
mechanism_names.discriminator: the planted arm reporting a warn line and the clean arm reporting the channel UNOBSERVABLE

mechanism_names.name_asserts: that device steadiness was certified before a measurement was admitted
mechanism_names.discriminator: the planted arm exiting non-zero with STEADY_UNCERTIFIED

mechanism_names.name_asserts: that every instrument in the tree was classified into Tank's six states
mechanism_names.discriminator: an instrument added to the tree and left unclassified turning the verdict from PASS to a finding

mechanism_names.name_asserts: that the EP's C ABI entry points were ENTERED and what they did there, so that 'Compute() ran and dispatched nothing' is a state the census can report rather than a gap
mechanism_names.discriminator: an observation that differs between a run whose Compute() dispatched and one whose Compute() returned early: compute_calls > 0 with dispatches_executed == 0. A mechanism that only reports compile_calls > 0 has not earned this name.

mechanism_names.name_asserts: that the nine environment switches were DISCLOSED as part of the run's frame, and — where a discrimination arm can exist — that the switch changed something the run produced
mechanism_names.discriminator: an observation whose CONTENT differs between the switch set and unset. For ONNXRUNTIME_EP_VULKAN_GEMV_PACKED specifically, no such observation exists today: the switch resolves to specialization constant 5 of q_gemv.comp and no artifact records a pipeline key or a spec constant, so disclosure is all this mechanism can currently do and disclosure is not R10 evidence.
